source_evidence.observation: The floating-point set is F = {m beta^e : m,e are integers, -beta^p < m < beta^p, and emin <= e <= emax}.
A nearest operation returns a member of F minimizing absolute error; a faithfully rounded operation has no other floating-point number between its rounded and exact real result.
The algorithm computes s <- x oplus y, t <- s ominus x, and e <- y ominus t, in that order.

source_evidence.anchor: definition of e(f) and Section 2 multiple-representation example
source_evidence.observation: The notation e(f) denotes the exponent in a representation f = m_f beta^(e(f)) satisfying equation (1); this exponent need not be unique, and Dekker's exponent condition is existential over feasible representations.
The section seeks a replacement for Dekker's base restriction and presents Theorem 2 as a generalization for arbitrary floating-point bases.
For x,y in F, nearest addition, faithful subtraction, and some representation of x satisfying |y| <= ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)), the computed s,e in F satisfy equation (3).

source_evidence.anchor: equation (8) and the proof of Theorem 2
source_evidence.observation: In the absence of overflow, |a-b| <= beta^p beta^(min(e(a),e(b))) implies a ominus b = a-b; the proof applies this to establish t = s-x.
Nearest addition gives |s-(x+y)| <= |y| in the nontrivial third proof case, because x itself is an available floating-point candidate.

source_evidence.anchor: completion of the proof of Theorem 2
source_evidence.observation: The proof establishes e = y-t exactly and hence, together with t = s-x, obtains s+e = x+y.

Faithful addition alone does not necessarily satisfy |x oplus y-(x+y)| <= |y|; therefore Theorem 2's nearest-addition hypothesis cannot simply be weakened to faithful addition while retaining equation (7).

binders: Fix the paper's floating-point system F with base beta, mantissa length p, and exponent range [emin,emax] (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1)).
Consider arbitrary inputs x,y in F (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).

Existentially choose a feasible representation x = m_x beta^(e(x)) satisfying equation (1); the theorem's bound is imposed using that representation's exponent (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, definition of e(f); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (7)).
Let s,t,e be computed sequentially by the three FastTwoSum instructions (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum lines 1-3).
hypotheses: x and y belong to F (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The circled-plus operation realizes nearest addition (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition).
The circled-minus operation realizes some faithful subtraction in both subtraction steps (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, faithful-rounding definition).
There exists a feasible representation of x for which |y| <= ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (7)).
No hypothesis |x| >= |y| is stated, and no normalized representation of x is required (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, multiple-representation discussion; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
conclusions: The stated conclusion is the exact real identity s + e = x + y, with s = x oplus y (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, equation (3); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The proof additionally establishes that line 2 is exact: t = s-x as a real subtraction (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8) and the three-case proof).
The proof additionally establishes that line 3 is exact: e = y-t as a real subtraction (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, completion of Theorem 2).
Consequently, e is exactly the addition residual (x+y)-s, not merely an approximation or bounded error estimate (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).
definitions_and_conventions: F consists of real values m beta^e with integer m,e, -beta^p < m < beta^p, and emin <= e <= emax (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1)).
A computed binary operation maps exact real arithmetic back into F through the paper's rounding map fl (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, paragraph following equation (1)).
Nearest addition minimizes absolute distance to the exact sum among all members of F; the definition does not prescribe a tie-breaking rule (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition display).
Faithful rounding means that no other floating-point number lies between the rounded and exact real result (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, faithful-rounding paragraph).
The exponent notation e(f) is representation-dependent and may have several feasible values for one floating-point number (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, definition of e(f) and x=3 example).

The returned residual e and the exponent notation e(x) are distinct uses of the same letter, distinguished in the paper by the argument parentheses (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum output; PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, definition of e(f)).
implicit_context: The proof uses 2 <= beta, inherited from beta being a floating-point base, rather than restating a domain for beta in Theorem 2 (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Case 3 immediately after equation (9)).

Equation (7) implies that Dekker's representation-dependent ordering e(x) >= e(y) is satisfiable, but this is a derived proof fact rather than an additional theorem hypothesis (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, first sentence of the proof; PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, equation (2)).

For beta in {2,3}, the paper states that equation (7) is equivalent to Dekker's original exponent condition, but Theorem 2 itself is not restricted to those two bases (PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, paragraph following the proof).

The exact-subtraction implication used by the proof is explicitly qualified by absence of overflow, although Theorem 2's displayed hypothesis list does not separately state that qualification (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8) and Theorem 2).
statement.algorithm_linkage: This contract concerns the original three-operation FastTwoSum variant: s <- x oplus y; t <- s ominus x; e <- y ominus t. Theorem 2 applies equation (7) to that exact instruction order and returns the pair (s,e) (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum algorithm; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
numerical_model: Exact symbols + and - denote real arithmetic, whereas oplus and ominus denote rounded operations with codomain F (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, operation model following equation (1)).

Line 1 must be nearest-rounded; requiring only faithful addition is insufficient for the theorem as stated (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, discussion of equation (10)).

Lines 2 and 3 require only faithful subtraction, and the proof shows that both particular subtractions are nevertheless exact under its bounds (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).
The theorem is formulated for the radix model of equation (1), not specifically for IEEE binary arithmetic (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1); PDF p. 4, printed p. 386, Section 3 introduction).
error_notions: The principal error notion is an error-free transformation: the rounded sum s and residual e add in exact real arithmetic to x+y (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, equation (3); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The residual is exact, e=(x+y)-s, because t=s-x and e=y-t are exact (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, proof of Theorem 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).
The proof uses the nearest-addition estimate |s-(x+y)| <= |y| in Case 3, but this bound is proof machinery rather than the theorem's stated final conclusion (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (9)).
norms: All magnitudes and errors in the selected result use scalar absolute value on real numbers; no vector, matrix, componentwise, or induced norm occurs (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equations (7)-(9); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).
constants_and_indexing: The exact threshold is ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)); the ceiling applies only to beta^p - beta/2, before multiplication by beta^(e(x)) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (7)).
The threshold is non-strict: |y| is allowed to equal ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (7)).

The exponent in the threshold belongs to an existentially selected representation of x, not necessarily a normalized or unique exponent (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, multiple-representation discussion; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The algorithm has exactly three numbered operations, with the rounded addition at line 1 and faithful subtractions at lines 2 and 3 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum algorithm).
Equation (8)'s exact-subtraction threshold is beta^p beta^(min(e(a),e(b))) and uses a non-strict inequality (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8)).
higher_order_terms: There are no big-O terms, omitted higher-order terms, or asymptotic qualifications: the final identity and both subtraction equalities are exact (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2 and equation (8); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).
exceptional_values: The model F contains finite real values of the form m beta^e and does not include NaN or infinity (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1)).
Zero is included by taking m=0, and Theorem 2 states no nonzero-input restriction (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).

Theorem 2 states no separate underflow exclusion; small values remain governed by the finite exponent-range model in equation (1) (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The general exact-subtraction implication is explicitly stated only in the absence of overflow (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8)).

undebatable_constraints: The algorithm must be the three-step FastTwoSum sequence s=x oplus y, t=s ominus x, e=y ominus t (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, FastTwoSum algorithm).

The inputs are scalar floating-point values x,y in F, and the relevant representation of x is existential rather than fixed as normalized (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, exponent discussion; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The magnitude condition is exactly |y| <= ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)) for that representation of x (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (7)).

Addition must be nearest-rounded and subtraction need only be faithfully rounded; faithful addition is not an interchangeable hypothesis (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, equation (10) discussion).

The required result is the exact identity s+e=x+y together with s=x oplus y, not merely an inequality or approximate residual (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, equation (3); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
The proof establishes exactness of both subtraction instructions, t=s-x and e=y-t (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equation (8) and proof; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion).

No condition |x| >= |y| and no restriction beta in {2,3} may be added to Theorem 2 (PDF p. 4, printed p. 386, Section 3 introduction; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, post-proof comparison).

ambiguities.issue: The treatment of overflow is not fully surfaced in the theorem statement.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (8), used to prove both exact subtraction steps, is introduced with the qualification 'in the absence of overflow,' while Theorem 2 does not list a separate overflow hypothesis (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2 and equation (8)).
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should either preserve this as an inherited no-overflow condition for the relevant subtractions or explicitly justify from the theorem hypotheses that those subtraction results cannot overflow; it should not silently claim IEEE exceptional-value behavior.

ambiguities.issue: The exponent e(x) is not a canonical function of x in the paper's model.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 2 explicitly gives one floating-point number several compliant exponents, and Theorem 2 says there is a representation of x satisfying equation (7) (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, multiple-representation example; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
ambiguities.impact: Replacing the existential representation witness with a normalized exponent or a fixed implementation exponent can strengthen or change the theorem.

ambiguities.evidence: Nearest addition is defined only by attaining the minimum absolute error over F; no ties-to-even or other tie rule is named (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, nearest-addition definition).
ambiguities.impact: The contract must allow any minimizing result in a tie and must not import an IEEE tie-breaking convention absent from the selected result.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'some faithful-subtraction' does not select a directed or nearest subtraction mode.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 2 asks only for some faithful-subtraction, using the paper's no-intervening-float definition of faithfulness (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, faithful-rounding definition; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2).
ambiguities.impact: The hypothesis must not be strengthened to nearest subtraction; exactness of the two executed subtractions is a proved consequence.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem inherits standard domain assumptions for beta and p instead of quantifying them explicitly.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (1) introduces beta as the base and p as the mantissa length, while the proof later explicitly uses 2 <= beta (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, equation (1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Case 3 after equation (9)).
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must supply the usual valid-radix and mantissa-length domains, but should label them inherited model assumptions rather than additional numerical restrictions peculiar to Theorem 2.

contract_plain_english: In the radix floating-point system F, take any x,y in F and run the original FastTwoSum instructions s=x oplus y, t=s ominus x, and e=y ominus t. Addition is nearest-rounded, while subtraction may be any faithful subtraction (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, rounding definitions and algorithm; PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, Theorem 2). If some feasible representation of x has exponent e(x) and satisfies |y| <= ceil(beta^p - beta/2) beta^(e(x)), then both subtraction instructions are exact and the returned values obey s+e=x+y with s=x oplus y (PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, equations (7)-(9); PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, proof completion). The exponent witness need not be normalized or unique, no |x|>=|y| condition is required, and the theorem is not restricted to bases 2 and 3 (PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, multiple-representation discussion; PDF p. 6, printed p. 388, post-proof comparison).
